overall: The AG found the Wilbraham Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice topic for its July 28 tree hearing continuation, but not for omitting a vote notice; no further remedy was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 28 notice topic on a continued tree hearing was insufficient because it did not state the board may take a vote.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find the notice insufficient because it failed to indicate that a vote may be taken.

allegations.summary: The July 28 notice topic, a continuation of a tree hearing with National Grid, was not specific enough to tell the public the board would discuss tree removal.
allegations.key_passage: we find it was insufficient to reasonably inform members of the public unfamiliar with the issue of the anticipated nature of the discussion.

allegations.summary: Complaint also named the Town Administrator and Tree Warden as violating the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law applies only to public bodies and public body members, not municipal employees.

allegations.summary: Complaint included alleged violations of G.L. c. 39, 23B, and 87, which the complainant conceded are outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Complainant acknowledges, however, that these allegations are outside the scope of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
